title: Global orientation and its normalization
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ be the separated finite-type $k$-scheme of the
affine-line datum, and let
$\kappa(t)\in H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},A(1))$ be the
Kummer class of the global coordinate
$t$. The boundary of $\kappa(t)$, determined through the
identification of [lem-pur-gysin-structure] (which gives the
support object $Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$
concentrated in degree zero), is the *global orientation* – a
morphism

$$
\operatorname{pur}_s:\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]
$$

in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=A$, where $Rs^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
of the zero section $s:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$, a closed
immersion whose ambient right adjoint exists unconditionally
([lem-exc-closed-ambient]) and preserves constructibility and
finite Tor amplitude, the open complement
$\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$ satisfying the
open-complement condition of
[lem-exc-closed-amplitude], [prop-exc-closed-tor] by
[lem-exc-open-complement-known],
with the shift $[2]$ and the twist
$(1)$. Its restriction to every geometric point $\bar y\to Y$ is
the normalized class $1\in H^2_{s(\bar y)}(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},\Lambda(1))$ of
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]. (Source: the affine-line
case of cohomological purity, obtained from the Kummer sequence and the
fundamental class of the zero section; Milne, Lectures on Etale
Cohomology, Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and 16.7, and Proposition 16.11
(the case $r=2c-1=1$ of the Gysin sequence of the divisor), with the
acyclicity of the affine line computed in Example 16.3, for the
relative form over a base scheme $Y$.)

external.place: Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and 16.7, and Proposition 16.11 (the case $r=2c-1=1$ of the Gysin sequence of the divisor), with the acyclicity of the affine line computed in Example 16.3, for the relative form over a base scheme $Y$.) The Kummer boundary defines the global morphism in the statement by [lem-pur-gysin-structure], [def-pur-affine-line-datum].

proof.text: Use the affine-line datum [def-pur-affine-line-datum]: write $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $Z=s(Y)$, $U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}$ and $F=A_X(1)$. Retain the datum's hypothesis $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$ and write $N=n/e\geq1$, $m=\ell^N$; the coefficient map is $\varphi(u)=\theta^{-1}(u\otimes1_A)$, and $\kappa(t)$ is the pro-etale comparison image of $\kappa_{\mathrm{et}}(t)=H^1(\varphi_U)(\delta_U(t))$. The zero section is a closed immersion, and its complement is quasi-compact (locally it is the principal open $D(t)$). The base is the algebraic closure of a finite field, $X$ is finite type, hence has a finite dimension bound $d\geq0$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] (choose $d=0$ if $X$ is empty), and the finite commutative ring $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell\ne p$. Thus [lem-exc-open-complement-known] supplies the open-complement condition of [def-exc-open-complement-bound], with $c=2d$. For the coefficient input to these bounds, [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](1),(3) and the datum's etale/pro-etale twist identification give an etale cover on which $F$ is the constant free rank-one $A$-module in degree zero. Thus $F$ is constructible, and for each $A$-module sheaf $M$, $F\otimes_A^L M$ is locally $M$ in degree zero; its Tor amplitude is $[0,0]$. The ambient etale right adjoint exists by [lem-exc-closed-ambient]; [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] and [prop-exc-closed-tor] then give respectively the bounded constructible and finite-Tor assertions in the statement. On the stated pro-etale coefficient category, $Rs^!$ is the transported etale adjoint, exactly as defined in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. In particular the ambient etale adjoint is not being asserted to be an adjoint on all pro-etale complexes.

source.place: §16, discussion preceding Theorem 16.7; the relative ambient bounds are the cited DAG statements

proof.text: The coordinate supplies the specified class $\kappa(t)\in H^1(U,A(1))$ of [def-pur-affine-line-datum]: the ordinary etale Kummer boundary of the unit $t\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$, followed by $H^1(\varphi_U)$ and then the datum's canonical comparison to the pro-etale site. Apply [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to the closed-open pair $(Z,X)$ and the finite-torsion twist $F$, and put $\alpha=\partial\kappa(t)\in H^2_Z(X,F)$. Let $K=Rs^!F[2]$. By [lem-pur-gysin-structure], $K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, is concentrated in degree zero, and the canonical identification of supported classes with sections of $\mathcal H^0(K)$ identifies $\alpha$ with a morphism $\operatorname{pur}_s:A_Y\to K$. Explicitly its degree-zero sheaf map sends $1$ to the section corresponding to $\alpha$. $A_Y$ also belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$: it is a finite constant, hence constructible, sheaf, and $A_Y\otimes_A^L M=M$ for every $A$-module sheaf $M$, so its Tor amplitude is $[0,0]$. Since $D^b_{ctf}$ is a full subcategory by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], this is a morphism in precisely the category in the statement. This constructs the global orientation with the displayed twist and shift.

source.place: Theorem 9.4 and its Ext description, Example 9.5; §16, Theorems 16.1 and 16.7

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar y=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$. Write $g:\bar y\to Y$, $h:X_{\bar y}\to X$, $h_U:U_{\bar y}\to U$, and $s':\bar y\hookrightarrow X_{\bar y}$ for the base changes along $g$, and $t_{\bar y}=h^*t$ for the coordinate of $X_{\bar y}=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$. Clause (4) of [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer], in its final sentence for a geometric point $g$ (no finite-type hypothesis on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$), says that the pullback of the Kummer class is the Kummer class; with $g'=h_U$ this is $h_U^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t_{\bar y})$. Both classes are formed by the formulas of [def-pur-affine-line-datum], with the same exponent $m=\ell^N$ (the hypothesis $e\mid n$ is retained, $N=n/e\geq1$, and $m$ is invertible on $U_{\bar y}$) and the same coefficient map $u\mapsto\theta^{-1}(u\otimes1_A)$. On the etale site, $\kappa_{\mathrm{et}}(t_{\bar y})=H^1(\varphi^{\mathrm{et}})(\delta_{U_{\bar y}}(t_{\bar y}))$ is the Kummer boundary of the unit $t_{\bar y}$ followed by $u\mapsto u\otimes1_A$; this is exactly the class $\kappa_A(t)$ used in step 7, and the datum's comparison identifies its pro-etale image with $\kappa(t_{\bar y})$. The base-change clause is a statement of the item's own unit, so no generic torsor functoriality is used.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, Example 9.5 and the Ext proof, pp. 66–67; Section 16, Kummer boundary

proof.text:
Functoriality in the pair in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] gives
$$h^*\alpha=h^*\partial\kappa(t)=\partial_{\bar y}h_U^*\kappa(t)=\partial_{\bar y}\kappa(t_{\bar y}).$$
This is pullback on supported classes. The identification [lem-pur-supported-hom] represents $\alpha$ by $m:s_*A_Y\to F[2]$. Its compatibility with pullback of the pair is precisely [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback]: under the canonical comparison of supported constants, $h^*\alpha$ is represented by $m'=h^*m$. Thus the supported boundary square is also a square of the corresponding derived morphisms; no naturality in the scheme is being inferred from naturality in $F$ alone.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, Example 9.5 and the Ext proof, pp. 66–67; Section 16, Kummer boundary

proof.text: The zero section and its base change are finite: on an affine chart they are $R[t]\to R[t]/(t)=R$, whose target is generated by $1$ as an $R[t]$-module. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] to this Cartesian square. Its canonical exchange, including its derived version, identifies $h^*Rs_*K$ with $Rs'_*g^*K$. These are comparisons on ordinary etale sites. For constant $A$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] supplies exact module inverse image and its ordinary pullback adjunction; the exchange respects the $A$-action because it is defined by that adjunction. Thus the comparison applies to the $A$-module complexes here. Set $K=Rs^!F[2]$ as above, $K'=Rs'^!h^*F[2]$ and let $\varepsilon:s_*K\to F[2]$ be the exceptional counit from [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. The identification of [lem-pur-gysin-structure](2) used in step 2 is the composite of degree-zero evaluation $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0K)=\operatorname{Hom}(A_Y,K)$, the exceptional adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(A_Y,Rs^!F[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(s_*A_Y,F[2])$ on the etale-origin objects of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and the supported-Hom identification [lem-pur-supported-hom] (this is how the source proof of that lemma, blueprint main-20261015, second paragraph, constructs it). So $\operatorname{pur}_s$ is the exceptional adjunct of $m$. Since $\nu^*$ is fully faithful on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and the site-comparison clause of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] carries the etale representative of $\alpha$ to $m$, both are images of their etale models; on those, [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] gives $m=\varepsilon\circ s_*\operatorname{pur}_s$.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, Example 9.5 and the Ext proof, pp. 66–67; Section 16, Kummer boundary

proof.text:
Let $\varepsilon':s'_*g^*K\to h^*F[2]$ be $h^*\varepsilon$ read through the exchange of the preceding step, and define $\beta:g^*K\to K'$ to be its exceptional adjunct. Naturality of that exchange gives $m'=\varepsilon'\circ s'_*g^*\operatorname{pur}_s$. The counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] says $\varepsilon_{s'}\circ s'_*\beta=\varepsilon'$, and functoriality gives
$$\varepsilon_{s'}\circ s'_*(\beta\circ g^*\operatorname{pur}_s)=\varepsilon'\circ s'_*g^*\operatorname{pur}_s=m'.$$
The same identity now gives $\operatorname{adj}(m')=\beta\circ g^*\operatorname{pur}_s$. By [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] this morphism represents the supported class $h^*\alpha$ computed above. This identifies the restriction of the orientation without assuming $\beta$ invertible. The fibre adjunction of [lem-exc-closed-ambient] imposes no finite-type-over-$k$ condition on $\Omega$. Finally [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] defines the chapter's pro-etale functor by transport from the etale adjoint; the pro-etale clause of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] and the site-comparison clause of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback], applied on $X_{\bar y}$ with full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], identify the transported restriction with this same boundary class.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, Example 9.5 and the Ext proof, pp. 66–67; Section 16, Kummer boundary

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] to $X_{\bar y}=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$ with support $Z_{\bar y}$ and the same finite-level coefficient twist. Its hypotheses hold: $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, $\ell$ is invertible in it, and $N=n/e\geq1$ has $\ell^N A=0$. Its coefficient sheaf is exactly $\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$, and its $\kappa_A(t)$ uses the same map $u\mapsto u\otimes1_A$ as the datum. Its residue isomorphism $\rho:H^2_{Z_{\bar y}}(X_{\bar y},A(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ sends $\partial_{\bar y}\kappa(t_{\bar y})$ to $1$, since $\operatorname{ord}_0(t_{\bar y})=1$. The preceding boundary square proves exactly the asserted normalization of $\operatorname{pur}_s$ at every geometric point. The cited support exactness and local-calculation statements explicitly include the finite-torsion pro-etale formulation, so this conclusion is in the site's coefficient category fixed in the item.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q128-7f6858fb9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the mathematics: AGENTS, stage-1, brief, GOAL, dag-sync, delivery-errors A–H, the packet, the report, the item and the new node in full, every cited statement, the unit sk-prop-a1-kummer, the main-20261015 blueprint item and lem-pur-gysin-structure/lem-pur-supported-hom with their proofs, Milne LEC §9 (Thm 9.4, Ext paragraph, Ex. 9.5, Prop. 9.6, proof on p. 67), and the earlier NE return. The statement is byte-identical to the blueprint and is not weakened; no SGA is cited. Steps 1, 2, 4 and 7 check against their hypotheses. The step-6 counit algebra checks: adj(m') = β∘g^*pur_s, with no invertibility of β assumed. The new lemma lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback is true: I tested h=id, empty Z, Z=X, degree 0, zero F or A, and non-finite-type geometric points. It is not a duplicate (I compared supported-hom, amb-closed-support-hom, supported-cup-functoriality, cartier-kummer, asd-supported-kummer and finite-exchange) and is strictly smaller than the item. I repaired three faults. (1) Step 3 (E5/C7) relied on an unstated identification of the pulled-back root torsor, an inverse-image-of-representable fact, through off-unit torsor functoriality. It now cites the unit's own prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer(4), whose geometric-point clause needs no finite type; there is no cycle, and the tool use for lem-sc-etale-torsor-h1-functoriality is withdrawn. (2) The new node's vague clause that the étale-to-pro-étale comparisons 'identify these two equalities' is replaced by a precise compatibility: χ^proet(ν^*α) = ν^{-1}χ(α)∘γ^{-1}, commuting with h^* and c. Step 6 now cites that clause plus thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison, which I add as an accepted tool use (the current blueprint proof also cites it). (3) Step 5 used m = ε∘s_*pur_s without saying that the identification in lem-pur-gysin-structure(2) is supported-Hom followed by the exceptional adjunction. This is now explicit, citing the main-20261015 blueprint proof of that lemma, with transport through full faithfulness of ν^*. The maintainer must make sure the split of lem-pur-gysin-structure constructs its identification exactly this way. All steps are under 2000 characters, proof_deps equals the union of uses, and the graph is acyclic. proof.text:
The Kummer boundary defines the global morphism in the statement by
[lem-pur-gysin-structure], [def-pur-affine-line-datum].
Its target is already a sheaf in degree zero, identified there with
$\Lambda_Y$ through the boundary $\delta$ of the localization triangle
of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] pushed forward to $Y$:
$\delta$ carries $R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)$, free of rank one on $\kappa(t)$
by [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](2), isomorphically onto
$\mathcal H^2(Rs^!\Lambda(1))$. So $\operatorname{pur}_s$, which sends
$1$ to the boundary of $\kappa(t)$, already maps $1$ to a generator of
this free rank-one sheaf.
The supported Cartier map of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] is natural
for the base changes of the zero section, and its geometric fibre is
the coordinate boundary. By [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]
that boundary is $1$. Consequently the morphism of degree-zero
sheaves has every stalk equal to the identity, and is an isomorphism.
The etale-origin comparison of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]
transports the assertion and its normalization to the stated site.
Uniqueness follows because a section of a sheaf is determined by its
stalks; this does not require a conservativity assertion for morphisms
of arbitrary derived objects.
